meta.inflation_note: Hint şirketleri enflasyon muhasebesi uygulamaz. Bu yüzden bütün şirketlerin özsermaye kârlılığı yıl sonu tüketici enflasyonuyla düzeltildi: 2021 için %5,66, 2022 için %5,72, 2023 için %5,69, 2024 için %5,22, 2025 için %1,33. data_notes: Fiyat, piyasa değeri, F/K ve PD/DD: TradingView tarayıcısı, 12 Kasım 2026. Evren 4.848 şirkettir: 3.171'i Ulusal Borsa'da (NSE, KOBİ pazarı dahil), 1.677'si yalnız Bombay Borsası'nda (BSE) işlem görüyor. Karşılaştırma: Ağustos 2026'da NSE'de 3.055 şirket vardı (NSE Market Pulse). BSE'de Eylül 2025'te 5.484 şirket kayıtlıydı, bunların 4.477'si işlem görüyordu (SEBI bülteni); iki borsada birden işlem gören şirketler bir kez sayılınca evren, fiilen işlem gören şirket sayısına yakındır. Hint şirketlerinin çoğunda mali yıl mart sonunda biter. Grafikte her şirketin kendi mali yılları yazar; enflasyon düzeltmesi aynı adı taşıyan takvim yılının oranıyla yapılır.

Hindistan'da bilanço yılda iki kez açıklanır (mart ve eylül sonu); haziran ve aralık çeyreklerinde yalnız gelir tablosu gelir. Kaynak bu yüzden 1.467 şirkette PD/DD alanını boş veriyordu (Hindustan Aeronautics ve Eicher Motors dahil). Bu şirketlerde PD/DD kaynaktaki son bilançodan hesaplandı (1.409 şirket), 10 şirkette ikinci kaynaktan alındı (stockanalysis.com), 48 şirkette son yıllık bilanço kullanıldı; hangisi olduğu şirketin sayfasında yazar. Denetim: Hindustan Aeronautics'te kaynak 8,07, şirketin 31 Mart 2026 bilançosuyla hesap 8,06; Eicher Motors'ta 8,30 ve 8,30.

Veri kaynağı 350 şirkette son 12 ayın kârını vermiyor. En büyükleri 2026'da halka arz edilen şirketler: Jio Platforms (28 Ekim 2026), Hindistan Ulusal Borsası (24 Eylül 2026) ve SBI Funds Management (21 Temmuz 2026). Bu şirketler zararda değil; kaynakta kâr verisi olmadığı için değerlendirilemedi ve sayfalarında 'kâr verisi eksik' yazar. Kaynağın F/K alanı boş, ama kârı belli olan 101 şirkette F/K aynı kaynaktan hesaplandı.
Bharti Airtel'de kaynağın F/K'sı (41,5) ikinci kaynağınkinden (Screener.in, 39,5) yaklaşık %6 yüksek; öbür dört büyük şirkette fiyat, piyasa değeri, F/K ve PD/DD %3 içinde tutuyor.
Beş yıllık oranlar: stockanalysis.com oran sayfaları. 43 adayın sayfası bulunamadı; bu şirketler 2. surda 'veri eksik' olarak durur.
Yıl sonu enflasyonu: Hindistan İstatistik Bakanlığı'nın (MOSPI) aralık ayı yıllık oranları, 2012 bazlı seri (2021-2025). Son yıllık oran: MOSPI, Eylül 2026, 2024 bazlı yeni seri (%5,54).
Bu kadar büyük bir borsada 3. sur okuması sırayla yapılır: önce fiyatı kale olmaya yetenler. Okunmayan şirket 'sırada' görünür.

en.name: India
en.exchange: National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) and BSE
en.inflation_note: Indian companies do not apply inflation accounting. The return on equity of every company was therefore adjusted by year-end consumer inflation: 5.66% for 2021, 5.72% for 2022, 5.69% for 2023, 5.22% for 2024 and 1.33% for 2025. For the last 12 months the most recently published annual rate (September 2026, 5.54%) was used.
data_notes: Price, market value, P/E and P/B: TradingView screener, 12 November 2026. The universe is 4,848 companies: 3,171 trade on the National Stock Exchange (NSE, including its SME board) and 1,677 on BSE only. For comparison: NSE had 3,055 listed companies in August 2026 (NSE Market Pulse). BSE had 5,484 listed companies in September 2025, of which 4,477 were traded (SEBI Bulletin); once companies traded on both exchanges are counted once, the universe is close to the number of companies that actually trade. 623 stocks with no price or market value were left out.
Most Indian companies end their fiscal year in March. The chart shows each company's own fiscal years; the inflation adjustment uses the rate of the calendar year with the same name.

In India balance sheets are published twice a year (end of March and end of September); the June and December quarters bring only an income statement. The source therefore left the P/B field empty for 1,467 companies (including Hindustan Aeronautics and Eicher Motors). For these companies P/B was derived from the latest balance sheet in the source (1,409 companies), taken from the second source for 10 companies (stockanalysis.com), and based on the last annual balance sheet for 48; the company's page says which. Check: for Hindustan Aeronautics the source gives 8.07, and the company's balance sheet of 31 March 2026 gives 8.06; for Eicher Motors 8.30 and 8.30.

For 350 companies the data source gives no profit figure for the last 12 months. The largest are companies that went public in 2026: Jio Platforms (28 October 2026), the National Stock Exchange of India (24 September 2026) and SBI Funds Management (21 July 2026). These companies are not loss-making; they could not be assessed because the source has no profit data, and their pages say 'profit data missing'. For 101 companies where the source's P/E field is empty but profit is known, the P/E was calculated from the same source.
For Bharti Airtel the source's P/E (41.5) is about 6% above the second source's (Screener.in, 39.5); for the other four large companies price, market value, P/E and P/B agree within 3%.
Five-year ratios: stockanalysis.com ratio pages. The pages of 43 candidates could not be found; these companies stay at Wall 2 as 'data missing'.
Year-end inflation: December annual rates from India's Ministry of Statistics (MOSPI), 2012-base series (2021-2025). Latest annual rate: MOSPI, September 2026, new 2024-base series (5.54%).
In a market this large, the Wall 3 reading is done in order: companies priced low enough to be castles come first. A company that has not been read yet is shown as 'in the queue'.
en.small_rule: Companies with a market value below 6 billion rupees (about 60 million US dollars) are left out.

ADANIPOWER.one: Hindistan'ın en büyük özel kömürlü elektrik üreticisi. Ürün emtia, sözleşmeler ihaleyle alınıyor; hendek zayıf olduğu için 3. suru geçemedi.
ADANIPOWER.business: Adani Power kömürle elektrik üretir ve çoğunu eyalet dağıtım şirketlerine uzun vadeli sözleşmelerle satar. Kurulu gücü 18.150 MW; kapasitenin yaklaşık %95'i uzun ve orta vadeli sözleşmelere bağlı. Mart 2026'da biten mali yılda 99,1 milyar kWh sattı; net kâr 129,7 milyar rupi oldu. Jharkhand'daki 1.600 MW'lık Godda santrali yalnız Bangladeş'e satış yapıyor.
ADANIPOWER.moat_text: Hendek zayıf; şirket bu ölçütü geçemedi. Elektrik emtiadır ve satış sözleşmeleri tarife ihalesiyle kazanılır. Üstünlük ölçekten, hazır santral sahalarından ve kömür tedarik düzeninden geliyor, ama tarifeyi şirket değil düzenleyici ve ihale belirliyor. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı son beş mali yılda %14,6 ile %49,3 arasında oynadı; yüksek yıllar geçmiş dönemlere ait tek seferlik gelirlerle şişti. Son 12 aydaki %20,4 de böyle: son çeyrekte 24,2 milyar rupilik geçmiş dönem geliri yazıldı.
ADANIPOWER.mgmt: Sermayenin %74,96'sı kurucu ortak Adani grubunda (Eylül 2026). Şirket 2015'ten beri temettü dağıtmadı. Kâr yeni santrallere gidiyor: 2032'ye kadar 23.720 MW yeni kömürlü kapasite hedefleniyor, toplam yatırım planı 2 trilyon rupinin üzerinde. Net borç Eylül 2026 sonunda 458,5 milyar rupi (Mart 2025 sonunda 310,2 milyar rupiydi); net borç/FAVÖK 1,88. Serbest nakit akışı son iki okumada eksi. Kasım 2024'te ABD savcıları grubun kurucusu Gautam Adani hakkında rüşvet iddiasıyla dava açtı; grup iddiaları reddediyor.
ADANIPOWER.latest: 23 Ekim 2026: Temmuz-Eylül 2026 çeyreğinde açıklanan hasılat 199,5 milyar rupi (+%39,4), net kâr 70,2 milyar rupi (+%141,5). Kârın içinde 24,2 milyar rupilik geçmiş dönem geliri ve 2,3 milyar rupilik vergi alacağı var; geçen yıl aynı çeyrekte 10,6 milyar rupi vergi gideri yazılmıştı. Bunlar hariç sürdürülen FAVÖK 63,2 milyar rupi (+%18,5). Satış 26,4 milyar kWh (+%11,5), kapasite kullanımı %70,1.
risks: Kâr tek seferlik kalemlerle şişiyor: geçmiş dönem gelirleri ve vergi alacakları çıkınca kazanç gücü açıklanan kârın belirgin altında.
Tarife ve geçmiş dönem alacakları düzenleyici ve mahkeme kararlarına bağlı; bir karar kârı iki yönde de oynatır.
Büyük yatırım planı borcu artırıyor ve serbest nakit akışını eksiye çeviriyor; ortağa nakit dönmüyor.
Bangladeş: Godda santralinin tek alıcısı Bangladeş'in elektrik kurumu. Temmuz 2026'da alacak yaklaşık 400 milyon dolardı ve fiyat formülü üzerine anlaşmazlık sürüyor.
Kömürlü üretim iklim politikalarının hedefinde; yeni santrallerin sözleşme süresi boyunca çalışacağı kesin değil.

en.one: India's largest private coal-fired power producer. Power is a commodity and contracts are won by tender; the moat is weak, so it failed Wall 3.
en.business: Adani Power generates electricity from coal and sells most of it to state distribution companies under long-term contracts. Its installed capacity is 18,150 MW; about 95% of the capacity is tied to long- and medium-term contracts. In the fiscal year that ended in March 2026 it sold 99.1 billion kWh; net profit was 129.7 billion rupees. The 1,600 MW Godda plant in Jharkhand sells only to Bangladesh.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; the company did not pass this criterion. Electricity is a commodity and sales contracts are won in tariff tenders. The advantage comes from scale, from ready plant sites and from the coal supply set-up, but the tariff is set by the regulator and the tender, not by the company. Real return on equity swung between 14.6% and 49.3% in the last five fiscal years; the high years were inflated by one-off income that belonged to earlier periods. The 20.4% of the last 12 months is the same: 24.2 billion rupees of prior-period income was booked in the last quarter.
en.mgmt: The founding shareholder, the Adani group, holds 74.96% of the capital (September 2026). The company has paid no dividend since 2015. Profit goes into new plants: the target is 23,720 MW of new coal-fired capacity by 2032, and the total investment plan is above 2 trillion rupees. Net debt was 458.5 billion rupees at the end of September 2026 (310.2 billion rupees at the end of March 2025); net debt/EBITDA is 1.88. Free cash flow was negative in the last two readings. In November 2024 US prosecutors brought a bribery case against the group's founder, Gautam Adani; the group rejects the allegations.
en.latest: 23 October 2026: In the July-September 2026 quarter reported revenue was 199.5 billion rupees (+39.4%) and net profit 70.2 billion rupees (+141.5%). The profit includes 24.2 billion rupees of prior-period income and a tax credit of 2.3 billion rupees; a tax charge of 10.6 billion rupees was booked in the same quarter last year. Excluding these, continuing EBITDA was 63.2 billion rupees (+18.5%). Sales were 26.4 billion kWh (+11.5%) and capacity utilisation was 70.1%.
risks: Profit is inflated by one-off items: without prior-period income and tax credits, earning power is clearly below reported profit.
Tariffs and prior-period claims depend on regulatory and court decisions; one ruling can move profit in either direction.
The large investment plan raises debt and turns free cash flow negative; no cash returns to shareholders.
Bangladesh: the only buyer of the Godda plant is Bangladesh's power board. In July 2026 the receivable was about 400 million dollars, and the dispute over the price formula continues.
Coal-fired generation is a target of climate policy; it is not certain that the new plants will run for the full term of their contracts.

BAJAJ_AUTO.business: Bajaj Auto motosiklet, üç tekerlekli ticari araç ve elektrikli scooter (Chetak) üretir; 79 ülkeye satar. İhracat hasılatın yaklaşık %40'ıdır. Mart 2026'da biten mali yılda konsolide satış 629,1 milyar rupi, net kâr 105,7 milyar rupi oldu. Şirket Kasım 2025'ten beri Avusturyalı motosiklet üreticisi KTM'in yaklaşık %75'ini kontrol ediyor ve kendi taşıt kredisi şirketini (Bajaj Auto Credit) işletiyor.
BAJAJ_AUTO.moat_text: Hendek dar. Üstünlük ölçekten ve dağıtımdan geliyor: şirket, Hindistan'da benzinli üç tekerlekli araç pazarının yaklaşık %70'ine sahip olduğunu, Hindistan'ın üç tekerlekli ihracatının %65'inden fazlasını yaptığını ve Afrika'da perakende payının %60'a yaklaştığını söylüyor. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılda %14,0'dan %21,3'e çıktı; son 12 ayda %28,4. Zayıf yan: Hindistan'da motosiklet pazarı çok rekabetli. Son çeyrekte yurt içi iki tekerlekli satışı yalnız %1,8 arttı ve şirket küçük motorlu (100 cc) sınıfta pay kaybediyor. Elektrikli scooter'da Chetak pazarın %23-24'ünü alıyor ama birinci değil.
BAJAJ_AUTO.mgmt: Kurucu ortaklar (Bajaj grubu) hisselerin %56'sını elinde tutuyor (Eylül 2026). Şirket Temmuz 2026'da temettü ve geri alımla yaklaşık 100 milyar rupi dağıttı; bu, bir önceki yılın kârının tamamıdır. 30 Eylül 2026'da 155 milyar rupi nakit fazlası vardı. Küçük kusur: zor durumdaki KTM'in devralınması ve kredi kolunun büyümesi bilançoyu ağırlaştırdı; konsolide borç Mart 2025'teki 93,6 milyar rupiden Eylül 2026'da 264,0 milyar rupiye çıktı. Kaynağın net borç/FAVÖK oranı 0,85.
BAJAJ_AUTO.latest: 27 Ekim 2026: Temmuz-Eylül 2026 çeyreğinde hasılat (konsolide olmayan) ilk kez 200 milyar rupiyi geçti: 200,0 milyar rupi (+%34). Net kâr 33,5 milyar rupi (+%35). Konsolide hasılat 251,3 milyar rupi (+%59), ana ortaklığa düşen net kâr 34,4 milyar rupi. Toplam satış 1.548.884 araç (+%19); ihracat 778.528 araç (+%40), yurt içi iki tekerlekli 607.416 araç (+%1,8). Chetak'ın hasılatı 20 milyar rupiyi geçti.
risks: Fiyat: F/K 23,3 ve PD/DD 8,2. Temkinli hesapla hisse adil değerin üzerinde; güvenlik marjı eşiği tutmuyor.

İhracat Afrika ve Latin Amerika'ya dayanıyor; bu ülkelerde kur ve döviz bulma sorunu satışı hızla düşürebilir. Zayıf rupi de bugünkü kârı destekliyor (şirketin gerçekleşen kuru bir yılda 85,6'dan 94,4'e çıktı).
KTM zor durumdayken devralındı; toparlanma uzarsa konsolide kârı ve borcu olumsuz etkiler.
Kredi kolu hızlı büyüyor (yönetilen kredi 200 milyar rupi, bir yılda %70'ten fazla artış); kredi kayıpları artarsa sermaye ister.
Son 12 ayın özsermaye kârlılığı geri alımdan ve güçlü ihracat döneminden destek alıyor; beş yıllık ortalama %20,0.

en.one: Maker of motorcycles and three-wheelers; about 40% of sales are exports. Narrow moat; passed the quality walls; waits at the gate on price.
en.business: Bajaj Auto makes motorcycles, three-wheeled commercial vehicles and electric scooters (Chetak) and sells in 79 countries. Exports are about 40% of revenue. In the fiscal year that ended in March 2026 consolidated sales were 629.1 billion rupees and net profit 105.7 billion rupees. Since November 2025 the company has controlled about 75% of the Austrian motorcycle maker KTM, and it runs its own vehicle finance company (Bajaj Auto Credit).
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage comes from scale and distribution: the company says it has about 70% of India's petrol three-wheeler market, makes more than 65% of India's three-wheeler exports, and has a retail share close to 60% in Africa. Real return on equity rose from 14.0% to 21.3% over five years; it was 28.4% in the last 12 months. The weak side: India's motorcycle market is very competitive. In the last quarter domestic two-wheeler sales rose only 1.8%, and the company is losing share in the small-engine (100 cc) class. In electric scooters Chetak takes 23-24% of the market but is not number one.
en.mgmt: The founding shareholders (the Bajaj group) hold 56% of the shares (September 2026). In July 2026 the company paid out about 100 billion rupees through dividends and a buyback; this is all of the previous year's profit. On 30 September 2026 it had surplus cash of 155 billion rupees. A small flaw: the takeover of the troubled KTM and the growth of the finance arm have made the balance sheet heavier; consolidated borrowings rose from 93.6 billion rupees in March 2025 to 264.0 billion rupees in September 2026. The source's net debt/EBITDA ratio is 0.85.
en.latest: 27 October 2026: In the July-September 2026 quarter revenue (standalone) crossed 200 billion rupees for the first time: 200.0 billion rupees (+34%). Net profit was 33.5 billion rupees (+35%). Consolidated revenue was 251.3 billion rupees (+59%) and net profit attributable to owners 34.4 billion rupees. Total sales were 1,548,884 vehicles (+19%); exports 778,528 vehicles (+40%), domestic two-wheelers 607,416 vehicles (+1.8%). Chetak revenue passed 20 billion rupees.
risks: Price: the P/E is 23.3 and the P/B 8.2. On the conservative calculation the share is above fair value; it does not meet the margin-of-safety threshold.

Exports rest on Africa and Latin America; exchange rates and shortages of hard currency in these countries can cut sales quickly. The weak rupee also supports today's profit (the company's realised rate went from 85.6 to 94.4 in a year).
KTM was taken over while in trouble; if the recovery takes long, it hurts consolidated profit and debt.
The finance arm is growing fast (loans under management of 200 billion rupees, up more than 70% in a year); if credit losses rise it will need capital.
Return on equity in the last 12 months is helped by the buyback and by a strong export period; the five-year average is 20.0%.

en.one: State company mining about three quarters of India's coal. Passed the quality walls; with a narrow moat the price falls short, waiting at the gate.
en.business: Coal India mines about three quarters of India's domestic coal and sells most of it to power plants (about 80% of shipments in September 2026). In the fiscal year that ended in March 2026 revenue was 1.68 trillion rupees and net profit 310.7 billion rupees. Most of the coal is sold under long-term agreements at the notified price; a small part goes through auctions at a premium.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The scale is real: about three quarters of the country's coal comes from this company, and real return on equity did not fall below 21.1% in five years. But the company cannot set its price in its own interest: in auctions the same coal sold at an average of 46% above the notified price in April-August 2026; because the main shareholder is the state, this difference stays with the power producers. The advantage rests on a public arrangement and its permanence is uncertain: the auction premium fell from 51% in 2024-25 to 38% in the first nine months of 2025-26. Real return on equity also came down from 51.6% (2023) to 21.6%. That is why we do not call it wide.
en.mgmt: The state holds 61.13% (September 2026); it sold a 2% stake in 2026. About half of profit is paid out as dividends (dividend yield 6.52%); a second interim dividend of 10.25 rupees per share was declared on 29 October 2026. The company has no net debt (net debt/EBITDA −1.34). The flaw: part of the profit is heading outside the core business. There is a target of 9.5 GW of renewable energy by 2030; coal gasification, critical minerals and an iron ore block are also on the agenda. Public policy drives these decisions. The board does not have the legally required number of independent directors; the auditor repeated this in its October 2026 review. With the state as controlling owner, this weakens protection of minority shareholders.
en.latest: 29 October 2026: In the July-September 2026 quarter revenue was 441.8 billion rupees (+21% year on year) total net profit 65.5 billion rupees (+57%) and the owners' share 65.2 billion rupees (+53%). Production was 151.4 million tonnes (+4%), shipments 186.3 million tonnes (+13%) and average revenue per tonne 2,346 rupees (+7%). In April-September 2026 revenue was 904.3 billion rupees and net profit 154.0 billion rupees (+19%); production was 321 million tonnes (−2%) and shipments 384.2 million tonnes (+8%). A second interim dividend of 10.25 rupees per share was declared.
risks: Price: the share clears the margin-of-safety threshold only if a wide moat is assumed. We judged the moat to be narrow; on that basis the price is not enough.

Part of profit is a non-cash entry: the stripping provision left from before 2022 is released to income each year (1,965 crore rupees in 2025-26, about 4.7% of pre-tax profit); the contribution ends when the provision is used up.
The auditor notes that the board lacks enough independent directors and its committees do not meet the legal make-up; the company has paid exchange penalties for this.

Dependence on public decisions: the main shareholder is the state and most customers are power plants. Not raising the notified price, opening the sector further to private miners, or instructions to invest outside the core business would affect profit directly.

The auction premium is volatile: 59% in August 2026, 38% in the first nine months of 2025-26. The most profitable part of earnings comes from here; when average revenue fell in 2025-26, net profit went from 354.5 billion rupees to 310.7 billion rupees.

en.one: India's state-owned maker of military aircraft and helicopters. Narrow moat; passed the quality walls; waits at the gate on price.
en.business: Hindustan Aeronautics builds fighter aircraft, helicopters and aircraft engines for the Indian armed forces, and maintains and repairs them. In the fiscal year that ended in March 2026 consolidated sales were 330.9 billion rupees and net profit 91.2 billion rupees. On 31 March 2026 the order book was about 2.54 trillion rupees, more than seven times one year of sales.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. This is the only large company in India that builds military aircraft and helicopters in series; the plants, the licences and decades of maintenance work are things a new rival cannot easily set up. In the year that ended in March 2026 about 62% of revenue came from repair and overhaul and 28% from manufacturing. Real return on equity stayed between 16.5% and 24.4% over five years and the last 12 months, and averaged 20.5%. The moat was not rated wide because the only customer is the state: it sets the price and the orders. Evidence of pricing power is weak: prices are approved by the state's pricing committee, and sales for April-September 2026 were booked at provisional 2024-25 prices because fixed-price quotations for the years after 2023 are not yet approved. We looked for the gross margin by year; it is not in the documents read. The company also depends on a foreign supplier: because General Electric engines are late, the first delivery of the Tejas Mk1A aircraft has been pending since February 2024; on 13 November 2026 deliveries had still not begun, and the first aircraft are expected to be handed over in January 2027.
en.mgmt: The Indian state holds 71.6% of the shares (September 2026). About one third of the profit is paid out as dividends: 45 rupees a share for fiscal 2025-26 (35 interim, 10 final); the source's payout ratio is 31%. The rest builds up as cash in the company. Debt is close to nil: about 0.09 billion rupees in September 2026 (net debt/EBITDA −5.65). Paid-up capital is unchanged (3.34 billion rupees); there is no share issue or buyback. Investment stays in the core business: 23.9 billion rupees of capital spending and 27.9 billion rupees of research and development in 2025-26 (about 8.4% of revenue); about 120 billion rupees of capital spending is planned to 2030. In November 2026 the takeover of the remaining 50% of the simulator-training venture HATSOFF for nil consideration was approved; the business is related to the core and small (net worth 0.35 billion rupees). We looked for share-based pay and for a company 'adjusted' profit measure; neither is in the documents read. We looked for the goodwill amount; it is not in the documents read. A new director of operations was appointed on 28 October 2026; another change in management was disclosed on 13 November 2026.
en.latest: 12 November 2026: In the July-September 2026 quarter consolidated revenue was 76.1 billion rupees (+14.8%) and net profit 19.4 billion rupees; a year earlier it was 16.7 billion rupees (+16%). Earnings per share were 28.94 rupees (24.96 a year earlier). EBITDA was 17.4 billion rupees (+11.6%) and the EBITDA margin 22.85% (23.51% a year earlier; 27.68% in the previous quarter). Other income was 9.9 billion rupees, 38.5% of pre-tax profit. In the first six months of the fiscal year revenue was 131.3 billion rupees (+14.7%), net profit 35.3 billion rupees (+15.5%) and earnings per share 52.71 rupees (45.65 a year earlier). On 30 September 2026 consolidated equity was 440.0 billion rupees. The auditor's opinion is unmodified.
risks: Price: the P/E is 33.6. On the conservative calculation the share is far above fair value; there is no margin of safety.

Single customer: almost all of the business depends on India's defence budget (exports are about 1.5% of revenue). The state is both owner and customer; it sets the orders, the price and the timing of payment. Sales for the last six months were booked at provisional prices; if the approved price differs, revenue is adjusted.

Delivery delays: 99 engines were ordered from General Electric for the Tejas Mk1A; 14 had arrived by the end of September 2026. In May the company said deliveries would start in August or September; on 13 November 2026 they had not. If the delay continues, revenue is pushed back and penalties may come up; the company does not disclose the penalty amount.

A large part of the profit comes from outside operations: in the last quarter other income was 38.5% of pre-tax profit (34.7% a year earlier). That income depends on the cash the company holds. The EBITDA margin also moves from quarter to quarter: it fell from 27.68% to 22.85%.

If the state gives more work to private companies and to projects with foreign partners, the company's position as sole producer weakens; for now the company is not part of the next-generation fighter (AMCA) project.

Off-balance-sheet obligations (pension deficit, contingent liabilities, guarantees) could not be checked in the company's results filing: the document could not be opened. In 2024-25 a provision of 8 billion rupees was booked for a Su-30 lost in an accident; such provisions can recur, depending on events.

en.latest: 12 October 2026: In the July-September 2026 quarter revenue was 356.2 billion rupees (+11.5% in rupees; +2.6% at constant exchange rates) and net profit 51.3 billion rupees (+21.2%). The company gave its growth outlook at constant exchange rates for fiscal 2027 as 2.5-4%; in April the range was 1-4%. The margin outlook is 17.5-18.5%. en.one: Leader of India's zinc market, a low-cost zinc and silver producer. It passed the quality walls; the price falls short, it waits at the gate.
en.business: Hindustan Zinc mines zinc, lead and silver from its mines in Rajasthan, processes them in its own smelters and sells them. Its share of India's primary zinc market is about 74%. In the fiscal year that ended in March 2026 revenue was 408.4 billion rupees and net profit 138.3 billion rupees; it produced 1,114 thousand tonnes of mined metal and 627 tonnes of silver. In April-September 2026 about 45% of profit came from silver.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage comes from cost and from the ore: in July-September 2026 the cost of producing a tonne of zinc (excluding royalty) was 703 dollars, 29% lower than a year earlier; the EBITDA margin was 62%. Metal reserves are 13.9 million tonnes and silver reserves 10.9 thousand tonnes. It holds about 74% of the country's primary zinc market. Real return on equity did not fall below 21.9% in five years. The weak side: what it sells is a commodity; the price is set by the London exchange and the silver market, not by the company. The 85.2% real return on equity of the last 12 months is the product of high metal prices. All the mines are in one state. That is why we do not call it wide.
en.mgmt: The main shareholder is the Vedanta group (the promoter stake was 60.71% in September 2026); the Indian state holds 27.92%. Vedanta sold shares twice in fiscal 2025-26. Profit goes largely to dividends: 10 rupees per share for 2025-26 (42.3 billion rupees in total). In some years the payout exceeded profit (303% of profit in 2022-23, 118% in 2024-25); this suggests that the decision follows the main shareholder's need for cash, and it was counted as a small flaw. The company plans to raise capacity by 2030 and to take silver capacity from 800 tonnes a year to 1,500 tonnes.
en.latest: 19 October 2026: In the July-September 2026 quarter revenue was 150.9 billion rupees (+77% year on year), EBITDA 92.9 billion rupees (+108%, margin 62%) and net profit 64.1 billion rupees (+142%). All three are quarterly records. Mined metal production was 271 thousand tonnes (+5%), refined metal 264 thousand tonnes (+7%) and silver 173 tonnes (+20%). Net profit for April-September 2026 was 118.8 billion rupees (+143%). On 30 September investments and cash were 174.4 billion rupees and borrowings 61.7 billion rupees.
risks: Price: the P/E of 11.5 looks low but the P/B is 8. On the conservative calculation the margin of safety is below the threshold.

Profit may be at the top of the metal price cycle: net profit in the last quarter was 2.4 times that of a year earlier, and about 45% of profit comes from silver. If the zinc or silver price falls, profit drops quickly; in 2023-24 net profit fell from 105.1 billion rupees to 77.6 billion rupees.
The main shareholder's need for cash: dividends above profit have been paid in the past. A similar decision would reduce the company's cash and raise its debt.
All mines and smelters are in Rajasthan. A decision on mining licences, the royalty rate, or water and energy would affect all production.
Growth investment: spending of more than 1 billion dollars a year is planned. Capacity that comes on stream when metal prices are low reduces returns.

en.one: India's second-largest IT services company. It passes the quality walls; it cut its growth outlook and waits at the gate on price.
en.business: Infosys sells software development, systems maintenance, consulting and outsourcing services to large companies. It earns its money through multi-year contracts, from the work of its engineers in India. In the fiscal year that ended in March 2026 revenue was 1.79 trillion rupees (20.2 billion dollars) and net profit 294.4 billion rupees. It has 88 clients that each bring more than 50 million dollars of work a year.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage comes from scale and from being embedded in clients' systems; moving the work to another firm is a chore. The evidence: real return on equity stayed between 22.0% and 27.2% in the last five fiscal years and was 23.1% in the last 12 months; the operating margin is 21.0%. The weak side: work is won by bidding, what is sold is engineer hours, and growth is very slow. Revenue at constant exchange rates rose only 1.5% in the last quarter. The effect of artificial intelligence on prices is also uncertain. That is why we did not class the moat as wide.
en.mgmt: The founding families hold 13.90% (September 2026); most of the shares are with institutional investors. Profit returns to shareholders: free cash flow in fiscal 2026 was 331.0 billion rupees (112.3% of net profit). A share buyback of 180 billion rupees was completed in December 2025. The buyback was made at 1,800 rupees per share; today's price is 1,143 rupees, so the buyback proved expensive. The company has no net debt (net debt/EBITDA −0.63); cash and investments were 430.8 billion rupees in March 2026.
en.latest: 23 October 2026: In the July-September 2026 quarter revenue was 492.4 billion rupees (+10.7% in rupees; +1.5% at constant exchange rates) and net profit 78.2 billion rupees (+6.2%). The operating margin was 21.0%. The total value of large contracts was 5.2 billion dollars; 62% of it was new work. The company lowered its growth outlook at constant exchange rates for fiscal 2027 from 1.5-3% to 1-2%; the margin outlook is 20-22%. An interim dividend of 26 rupees per share was declared.
risks: Price: the P/E is 15.1 and the P/B 4.7. On the conservative calculation the share is above fair value; there is no margin of safety.
The growth outlook was lowered: 1-2% at constant exchange rates for fiscal 2027. Most of the growth in rupees comes from the exchange rate.
Artificial intelligence can reduce both the price and the volume of the engineer hours the company sells; the net effect is not yet clear.

Dependence on the United States: on 7 October 2026 US officials barred Infosys and seven other firms from an immigration programme (PERM). The company said it does not expect a significant effect, but costs rise if visa and immigration rules tighten.
The buyback was made far above today's price; this stands as a flaw in capital allocation.

en.one: India's largest cigarette maker. Wide moat, but cigarette tax rose for good and profit fell. For that reason it was not taken to the price test.
en.business: ITC works in four lines: cigarettes, packaged food and personal care products, agricultural trading, and paper and packaging. In the fiscal year that ended in March 2026 consolidated sales were 788.7 billion rupees and net profit 210.2 billion rupees. The main source of profit is cigarettes: in the July-September 2026 quarter about three quarters of segment profit came from cigarettes.
en.moat_text: The moat is wide. ITC is the country's largest maker and seller of cigarettes; the brands, the distribution network and the advertising ban make it very hard for a new rival to enter. This strength shows in return on equity: real return on equity stayed between 18.3% and 25.9% over five years and averaged 21.8%. The weak side is clear: most of the profit comes from one product, and the state sets the tax on that product. After the tax increase of 1 February 2026 the quarterly profit of the cigarette business fell 27.2%. Food and other consumer products are growing fast, but their profit is still small.
en.mgmt: The company has no controlling shareholder. In September 2026 domestic institutions held 49.8% of the shares and foreign institutions 33.2%. The largest shareholder, British American Tobacco, sold a 2.5% stake in May 2025 and brought its holding below 23%. Almost all of the profit is paid out as dividends: the payout ratio is 96% and the dividend yield 5.1%. There is no net debt (net debt/EBITDA −0.86).
en.latest: 2 November 2026: In the July-September 2026 quarter net profit (standalone) was 41.4 billion rupees; a year earlier it was 51.8 billion rupees (−20.1%). Consolidated net profit was 42.3 billion rupees (−18.5%). Gross revenue including taxes rose 46.6%, net revenue rose only 3.1%; EBITDA fell 17.4%. Profit of the cigarette business fell to 38.1 billion rupees (−27.2%). In food and other consumer products revenue rose 15.7% and profit 27.8%; profit of the paper business rose 47.6%. The company says cigarettes improved compared with the previous quarter.
risks: Tax: since 1 February 2026 cigarettes carry an excise duty of 2,050 to 8,500 rupees per thousand sticks depending on length, and the goods and services tax (GST) rose from 28% to 40%. Profit fell by more than 20% in each of the last two quarters; trailing 12-month profit and return on equity may decline because of this.
Dependence on one product: about three quarters of segment profit comes from cigarettes.
Price increases can push consumers to illicit cigarettes; this is why the company raises prices in steps.
British American Tobacco is reducing its stake; new block sales can weigh on the share price.
Price: on the conservative calculation the share is above fair value; it does not meet the margin-of-safety threshold.

NESTLEIND.one: Maggi, Nescafé ve KitKat'ın Hindistan'daki sahibi. Hendek geniş, kalite surlarını geçti; fiyat çok pahalı olduğu için kapıda bekliyor.
NESTLEIND.business: Nestlé India hazır erişte ve sos (Maggi), kahve (Nescafé), çikolata (KitKat), süt ürünleri (Milkmaid) ve bebek maması (Cerelac) satar. İsviçreli Nestlé'nin bağlı ortaklığıdır. Mart 2026'da biten mali yılda satış 230,7 milyar rupi, net kâr 35,4 milyar rupi, FAVÖK marjı %23,0 oldu. Şirket ürünlerini 28 ülkeye de ihraç ediyor.
NESTLEIND.moat_text: Hendek geniş. Üstünlük markalardan ve dağıtımdan geliyor: Maggi kendi sınıfında pazar lideri, öbür markalar da onlarca yıldır rafta. Şirket ana ortağın markalarını, teknolojisini ve araştırmasını kullanıyor. Fiyatlama gücü rakamlarda görünüyor: FAVÖK marjı %23, reel özsermaye kârlılığı son okumalarda %67 ile %97 arasında. Bu kadar yüksek oranın bir nedeni özsermayenin küçük olmasıdır; şirket kârın çoğunu dağıtıyor. Bir rakibin aynı markaları ve dağıtımı kurması yıllar ve büyük sermaye ister.
NESTLEIND.mgmt: Hisselerin %62,8'i Nestlé S.A.'nın elinde (Eylül 2026). Kârın yaklaşık üçte ikisi temettü olarak dağıtılıyor (dağıtım oranı %66); kalanı kapasiteye gidiyor: şirket Hindistan'daki onuncu fabrikasını kuruyor. Borç düşük: Mart 2026'da 4,4 milyar rupi (net borç/FAVÖK −0,22). Küçük ortak açısından kusur: şirket ana ortağa net satışın %4,5'i kadar lisans bedeli ödüyor (2026 mali yılında 10,2 milyar rupi). en.one: The owner of Maggi, Nescafé and KitKat in India. Wide moat; passed the quality walls; waits at the gate because the price is very high.
en.business: Nestlé India sells instant noodles and sauces (Maggi), coffee (Nescafé), chocolate (KitKat), milk products (Milkmaid) and baby food (Cerelac). It is a subsidiary of Switzerland's Nestlé. In the fiscal year that ended in March 2026 sales were 230.7 billion rupees, net profit 35.4 billion rupees and the EBITDA margin 23.0%. The company also exports to 28 countries.
en.moat_text: The moat is wide. The advantage comes from the brands and the distribution: Maggi is the market leader in its category, and the other brands have been on the shelf for decades. The company uses the parent's brands, technology and research. Pricing power shows in the figures: the EBITDA margin is 23%, and real return on equity was between 67% and 97% in recent readings. One reason the ratio is so high is that equity is small; the company pays out most of its profit. Building the same brands and distribution would take a rival years and a large amount of capital.
en.mgmt: Nestlé S.A. holds 62.8% of the shares (September 2026). About two thirds of the profit is paid out as dividends (payout ratio 66%); the rest goes into capacity: the company is building its tenth factory in India. Debt is low: 4.4 billion rupees in March 2026 (net debt/EBITDA −0.22). A flaw from the minority shareholder's point of view: the company pays the parent a licence fee of 4.5% of net sales (10.2 billion rupees in fiscal 2026). Management proposed raising this rate to 5.25% over five years; shareholders rejected the proposal.
en.latest: 15 October 2026: In the July-September 2026 quarter total sales rose 20.5% and domestic sales 20.4%. Net profit was 10.3 billion rupees; a year earlier it was 7.5 billion rupees (+36.3%). The EBITDA margin was 23.8%. The cost of materials fell from 45.5% of sales to 43.1%; spending on advertising and marketing rose 46%. The company says growth came across all product groups and from volume. In the first six months of the fiscal year net profit was 20.0 billion rupees (+41.7%).
risks: Price: the P/E is 59.7 and the P/B 42.2. On the conservative calculation the share is far above fair value; there is no margin of safety.
Raw material prices: if milk, coffee, cocoa and wheat become more expensive the margin narrows.
Licence fee: an increase in the rate paid to the parent may be sought again; this reduces the profit left for minority shareholders.
Return on equity looks very high because equity is small; the ratio fell from 97% to 67% over five years.
watch: EBITDA margin and raw material cost

en.one: India's largest IT services company. It passes the quality walls; growth is slow and it waits at the gate on price.
en.business: TCS sells software development, systems maintenance, consulting and business process services to large companies around the world. It earns its money through multi-year contracts, from the work of its engineers in India. In the fiscal year that ended in March 2026 revenue was 2.67 trillion rupees and net profit 494.5 billion rupees. It had 598,056 employees at the end of September 2026.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage comes from scale and from being embedded in clients' systems over many years: moving the work to another firm is costly and risky for the client. The figures show it: real return on equity stayed between 35.7% and 50.2% in the last five fiscal years and was 37.9% in the last 12 months; the operating margin is 24.0%. The weak side: work is won by bidding and what is sold is engineer hours. Growth at constant exchange rates has slowed to 2.8% a year. It is not clear how far artificial intelligence will push down the price of those hours. That is why we did not class the moat as wide.
en.mgmt: The founding shareholder, the Tata group, holds 71.77% of the capital (September 2026). Most of the profit is paid out to shareholders: 395.7 billion rupees in total in fiscal 2026, a payout ratio of 81%. The company has no net debt (net debt/EBITDA −0.54). In fiscal 2026 management cut the workforce by 23,460 people and set aside 13.9 billion rupees for it. In October 2026 it announced the decision to buy MHP, Porsche's consulting company; the price is not in the sources we read.
en.latest: 8 October 2026: In the July-September 2026 quarter revenue was 731.9 billion rupees (+11.2% in rupees; +2.8% at constant exchange rates) and net profit 138.8 billion rupees. Net profit excluding one-off items was 129.0 billion rupees in the same quarter a year earlier. The operating margin was 24.0%. The total contract value of new work won was 9.6 billion dollars. Annualised artificial intelligence revenue passed 3.1 billion dollars (more than 10% of revenue). An interim dividend of 12 rupees per share was declared.
risks: Price: the P/E is 17.0 and the P/B 7.4. On the conservative calculation the share is above fair value; there is no margin of safety.
Artificial intelligence can reduce both the price and the volume of the engineer hours the company sells. The company also earns revenue in this field, but the net effect is not yet clear.
Growth is slow: 2.8% a year at constant exchange rates. Most of the growth in rupees comes from the exchange rate; if the rupee strengthens, revenue and the margin fall.
Revenue in North America grew only 1.5% at constant exchange rates. Budget cuts and work visa restrictions there affect the business directly.
The MHP acquisition is outside the company's usual scale; its price and return are not yet known.
watch: Revenue growth at constant exchange rates

en.one: A Mumbai-based construction contractor. It wins work by tender and contract, and a large part of its orders comes from its own promoter group; it did not pass the moat criterion.
en.business: Garuda Construction is a building contractor for residential, commercial and infrastructure projects; it also does operation and maintenance and building services work. In the year ended March 2026 revenue was 530.7 crore rupees (5.3 billion rupees) and net profit 122.5 crore; a year earlier they were 225.7 and 49.8 crore. The order book was 4,337 crore rupees at 31 December 2025. The company listed in October 2024; the controlling shareholder is the PKH Ventures group (67.6%).
en.moat_text: There is no moat; the company did not pass the third wall. A building contractor wins work by tender and bid and has no lasting pricing power. The operating margin is about 30%, far above similar contractors (10-17%); but that margin cannot be taken as proof of an advantage, because a large part of the orders comes from companies of the promoter group: the group wins the tender or acts as developer and gives the construction to Garuda. According to a review on an investor forum, more than half of the order book is from related parties (this share could not be confirmed from a company document). The rating agency Infomerics pointed to slow collections: the working capital cycle lengthened from 248 to 405 days, and projects worth 1,537 crore rupees are waiting for official approvals. Real return on equity was between 20% and 57% over five years.
en.mgmt: The controlling shareholder is the PKH Ventures group; the chairman and managing director is Pravin Kumar Agarwal. The listing raised 163 crore rupees of capital (fiscal 2025). Dividends are negligible; profit stays in the company and much of it is tied up in receivables: at 31 March 2026 trade receivables were 148.8 crore in the consolidated accounts and 240.4 crore rupees in the standalone accounts, against equity of 454.4 crore. The share count rose 24.5% in five years. In December 2025 the company asked shareholders for authority to issue up to 500 crore rupees of new shares (forum source). A note to the 2026 year-end results says trade payable and advance balances are 'subject to confirmation and reconciliation'. Debt is low: 12 crore rupees at 31 March 2026; 53 crore in September 2026 according to the source. We looked for share-based pay, goodwill and off-balance-sheet obligations; they are not in the documents read.
en.latest: 4 November 2026: The company reported the July-September 2026 quarter (read from secondary sources). Total income was 172.6 crore rupees (+45.7%) and net profit 40.6 crore rupees (+49.7%). In the first half total income was 348.2 crore (+42.1%) and net profit 82.1 crore (+49.0%). Year-end results announced on 18 May 2026: revenue 530.7 crore, net profit attributable to owners 122.5 crore, earnings per share 13.17 rupees; net cash from operations 78.4 crore rupees.
risks: A large part of the orders comes from companies of the promoter group; an outsider cannot see whether prices and collections are on market terms.
Profit turns into cash slowly: operating cash flow was negative in fiscal 2025 (−111 crore rupees according to the source) and debtor days are 165.

en.one: A small company selling medical equipment and diagnostic supplies to healthcare institutions. A third of revenue comes from one customer, profit is not turning into cash and sales halved in the latest quarter; it did not pass the moat criterion.
en.business: One Global Service Provider sells medical equipment, laboratory analysers, reagents and software to hospitals and public health programmes; it also runs diagnostic laboratories. It used to be a textile company and moved into healthcare after a change of management. Revenue was 6 crore rupees in fiscal 2022; a merger and institutional contracts took it to 498.8 crore rupees (5.0 billion rupees) in the year to March 2026, with net profit of 69.5 crore rupees.
en.moat_text: There is no moat; the company did not pass the third wall. The business is selling equipment and supplies made by others to institutions; it is won by contract and no figure shows a lasting advantage. About a third of fiscal 2026 revenue came from a single diagnostic services customer. Revenue grew 80-fold in four years and then halved in the July-September 2026 quarter (66.5 crore; 135.0 crore a year earlier): earnings are not predictable (C score 0). Trade receivables were 216.6 crore rupees at 31 March 2026; that is 85% of total assets and about four times the 57.7 crore of a year earlier. Real return on equity ranged from 13% to 57% over five years. Free cash flow was negative in the last two periods.
en.mgmt: The ownership has changed often: the promoters' stake was 15.05% in March 2025, 66.24% in September 2025 and is 68.40% today. The share count rose 175% in five years. In November 2026 a postal ballot was opened: shareholders are voting on converting a loan into shares and on the chairman's pay and reappointment; new shares issued through a share swap are awaiting listing. The dividend is very small (yield 0.26%). Profit is piling up in receivables; operating cash flow is negative (−10.9 crore rupees according to a secondary source). In May 2026 the year-end results filing was resubmitted because of a clerical error. The company's own document (exchange filing) could not be opened; share-based pay, goodwill and off-balance-sheet obligations could not be checked.
en.latest: 4 November 2026: The company reported the July-September 2026 quarter (read from a secondary source, standalone accounts). Sales were 66.45 crore rupees, 50.8% below the 134.98 crore of a year earlier. Net profit was 8.29 crore rupees (19.79 crore; −58.1%). The operating margin was 16.7% (19.3% a year earlier).
risks: A third of revenue comes from one customer and receivables are 85% of assets; if collections slip, the profit stays on paper.
In the latest quarter sales halved and profit fell 58%; nothing shows that the growth of earlier years is continuing.

ASHOKA.one: Yol ve altyapı müteahhidi. Son 12 ayın kârı otoyol satışından gelen tek seferlik kazanç; iş ihaleyle alınıyor, hendek yok. 3. suru geçemedi.
ASHOKA.business: Ashoka Buildcon, Hindistan'da otoyol, demiryolu, elektrik iletim hattı ve bina inşa eder; ayrıca kendi yaptığı bazı yolları işletir. İş kamu ihaleleriyle alınır. 30 Eylül 2026'da elindeki sipariş 159,6 milyar rupi: %38,7'si yol yapımı, %23,9'u elektrik iletim ve dağıtım, %10,4'ü demiryolu. Temmuz-Eylül 2026 çeyreğinde konsolide hasılat 15,0 milyar rupi.
ASHOKA.moat_text: Hendek yok; şirket 3. suru bu yüzden geçemedi. İş ihaleyle, en düşük teklifi veren alır; müteahhitlik kolunda FAVÖK marjı %10 dolayında (Temmuz-Eylül 2026'da %9,9). Sayfadaki düşük F/K (1,39) ve yüksek özsermaye kârlılığı ana işten gelmiyor: Ekim-Aralık 2025 çeyreğinde şirket beş paralı otoyol şirketini Maple Infrastructure Trust'a 18,1 milyar rupiye sattı ve o çeyrekte 23,8 milyar rupi tek seferlik kazanç yazdı. O çeyreğin net kârı 21,1 milyar rupi; son dört çeyreğin toplamı yaklaşık 22,7 milyar rupi. Yani satış kazancı çıkınca son 12 ayda kâr kalmıyor. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı da buna göre oynak: beş yılda %10,5 ile %54,6 arası.
ASHOKA.mgmt: Kurucu ortakların payı %54,47 (Eylül 2026). Şirket 2019'dan beri temettü dağıtmıyor. Otoyol satışından gelen para borca gitti: konsolide borç Eylül 2025'teki 49,1 milyar rupiden Eylül 2026'da 27,8 milyar rupiye indi; bu olumlu. Altı yol projesinin daha satılması bekleniyor. Kâr tek seferlik ve faaliyet dışı kaynaktan geldiği için kazancın öngörülebilirliği ölçütünü de geçemedi.
ASHOKA.latest: 5 Kasım 2026: Temmuz-Eylül 2026 çeyreğinde konsolide hasılat 15,0 milyar rupi (yıllık −%18,7). Şirket 1,19 milyar rupi net zarar yazdı (geçen yıl 0,91 milyar rupi kâr). Neden: 3,19 milyar rupilik tek seferlik gider; haber özetine göre bunun 2,37 milyar rupisi değer düşüklüğü, 0,82 milyar rupisi bakım kaynaklı zarar. Tek seferlik gider öncesi vergi öncesi kâr 1,91 milyar rupi (geçen yıl 2,84 milyar). Nisan-Eylül 2026 net kârı 82 milyon rupi (geçen yıl 3,18 milyar). Sipariş tutarı 159,6 milyar rupi.
risks: Sayfadaki F/K (1,39) yanıltıcıdır: son 12 ayın kârı beş otoyol şirketinin satışından gelen 23,8 milyar rupilik tek seferlik kazançtan oluşuyor. Bu kazanç dönemden çıkınca F/K çok yükselecek; son iki çeyreğin toplam kârı 82 milyon rupi.
Ana iş küçülüyor: Nisan-Eylül 2026'da konsolide hasılat %19,6 düştü. Yönetim 2026-27 mali yılı için yaklaşık %20 büyüme hedeflemişti.

İş kamu ihalelerine ve kamu kurumlarının ödemelerine bağlı. Şubat 2026'daki toplantıda yönetim, karayolları kurumu (NHAI) ile ilgili bir konunun mahkemede durdurulduğunu, Bihar'daki bir soruşturmanın ise önemli bir mali etkisinin beklenmediğini söyledi.
Tek seferlik giderler yineleniyor: son iki yılın Temmuz-Eylül çeyreklerinde 2,19 ve 3,19 milyar rupi yazıldı. Kalan yol varlıklarının satışı gecikirse yeni değer düşüklüğü gelebilir.

en.one: Road and infrastructure contractor. Last 12 months' profit is a one-off gain from toll-road sales; work is won by tender. Did not pass Wall 3.
en.business: Ashoka Buildcon builds highways, railways, power transmission lines and buildings in India; it also operates some of the roads it built. Work is won in public tenders. On 30 September 2026 its order book was 159.6 billion rupees: 38.7% road construction, 23.9% power transmission and distribution, 10.4% railways. Consolidated revenue in the July-September 2026 quarter was 15.0 billion rupees.
en.moat_text: There is no moat; this is why the company did not pass Wall 3. Work is won by tender and goes to the lowest bidder; the EBITDA margin of the contracting arm is around 10% (9.9% in July-September 2026). The low P/E on the page (1.39) and the high return on equity do not come from the core business: in the October-December 2025 quarter the company sold five toll-road companies to Maple Infrastructure Trust for 18.1 billion rupees and booked a one-off gain of 23.8 billion rupees in that quarter. Net profit in that quarter was 21.1 billion rupees; the total of the last four quarters is about 22.7 billion rupees. So once the sale gain is taken out, no profit is left in the last 12 months. Real return on equity is volatile for the same reason: between 10.5% and 54.6% over five years.
en.mgmt: The founders hold 54.47% (September 2026). The company has paid no dividend since 2019. The money from the toll-road sale went to debt: consolidated debt fell from 49.1 billion rupees in September 2025 to 27.8 billion rupees in September 2026; this is positive. Six more road projects are expected to be sold. Because profit came from a one-off, non-operating source, the company also did not pass the predictability-of-earnings criterion.
en.latest: 5 November 2026: In the July-September 2026 quarter consolidated revenue was 15.0 billion rupees (−18.7% year on year). The company booked a net loss of 1.19 billion rupees (a profit of 0.91 billion rupees a year earlier). The reason: a one-off expense of 3.19 billion rupees; according to the news summary, 2.37 billion rupees of it is impairment and 0.82 billion rupees is maintenance-related losses. Profit before tax and before the one-off expense was 1.91 billion rupees (2.84 billion a year earlier). Net profit for April-September 2026 was 82 million rupees (3.18 billion a year earlier). The order book stood at 159.6 billion rupees.
risks: The P/E on the page (1.39) is misleading: the last 12 months' profit consists of a one-off gain of 23.8 billion rupees from the sale of five toll-road companies. Once this gain drops out of the period the P/E will rise sharply; total profit in the last two quarters was 82 million rupees.
The core business is shrinking: consolidated revenue fell 19.6% in April-September 2026. Management had targeted growth of about 20% for fiscal 2026-27.

The business depends on public tenders and on payments by public bodies. On the February 2026 call management said a matter involving the highways authority (NHAI) had been stayed in court and that an investigation in Bihar was not expected to have a material financial impact.

One-off expenses keep recurring: 2.19 and 3.19 billion rupees were booked in the July-September quarters of the last two years. If the sale of the remaining road assets is delayed, new impairments may follow.

HINDUNILVR.one: Hindistan'ın en büyük temizlik, kişisel bakım ve gıda markaları şirketi. Hendek geniş; fiyat çok pahalı olduğu için kapıda bekliyor.
HINDUNILVR.business: Hindustan Unilever deterjan, sabun, şampuan, cilt bakımı, çay, kahve ve hazır gıda satar. Yılda yaklaşık 85 milyar paket ürünü yaklaşık 9 milyon satış noktasına ulaştırır. Mart 2026'da biten mali yılda hasılat 637,6 milyar rupi, FAVÖK marjı %23,6 oldu. Yıllık satışı 10 milyar rupiyi aşan 21 markası var.
HINDUNILVR.moat_text: Hendek geniş. Üstünlük markalardan ve dağıtımdan geliyor: 21 büyük marka ve yaklaşık 9 milyon satış noktasına ulaşan bir ağ. Bir rakibin aynı ağı kurması yıllar ve büyük sermaye ister. Fiyatlama gücü marjda görünüyor: FAVÖK marjı %22-24 aralığında. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı son beş mali yılda %12,0 ile %19,6 arasında kaldı, son 12 ayda %15,2. Zayıf yanı: son iki yılda büyüme cılızdı; şirket büyümeyi satın aldığı yeni markalarda (Minimalist, OZiva) arıyor. Reel kârlılık 2. surun eşiklerine yakın.
HINDUNILVR.mgmt: Sermayenin %61,90'ı ana ortak Unilever'de (Eylül 2026). Kârın büyük bölümü temettü olarak dağıtılıyor: 2026 mali yılı için hisse başına 41 rupi, toplam 96,3 milyar rupi. Şirketin net borcu yok (net borç/FAVÖK −0,54). Dondurma işi Aralık 2025 çeyreğinde ayrı bir şirkete (Kwality Wall's) devredildi; Minimalist ve OZiva satın alındı, Pureit satıldı. Yönetim yatırım harcamasını hasılatın %2'sinden %3'üne çıkarmayı planlıyor.
HINDUNILVR.latest: 28 Ekim 2026: Temmuz-Eylül 2026 çeyreğinde hasılat 180,7 milyar rupi. Şirketin açıkladığı temel satış büyümesi %15 ile son 14 çeyreğin en yükseği; satış hacmi %7 arttı. FAVÖK 40,9 milyar rupi (+%8), FAVÖK marjı %22,6 (geçen yıla göre 1,4 puan düşük). Net kâr 28,0 milyar rupi ile geçen yılla aynı; istisnai kalemler hariç %9 arttı. Hisse başına 19 rupi ara temettü açıklandı.
risks: Fiyat: sayfadaki F/K 30,8, dondurma işinin ayrılmasından gelen yaklaşık 46 milyar rupilik tek seferlik kazancı içeren kârla hesaplı. Bu kazanç çıkarılınca çarpan daha da yüksek (Screener.in'de 42,0). Güvenlik marjı yok.
Marj baskısı: son çeyrekte FAVÖK marjı 1,4 puan geriledi; girdi maliyetleri yüksek. Büyüme hacimle geliyor, kâr aynı hızla artmıyor.
Reel özsermaye kârlılığı ortalaması 2. surun eşiğinde. Enflasyon yükselirse ya da kâr gerilerse şirket kalite surunda elenebilir.
Yeni ve internetten satan markalar ile hızlı teslimat uygulamaları, dağıtım ağının sağladığı üstünlüğü zayıflatabilir.
Ana ortak Unilever çoğunluk sahibi; temettü ve satın alma kararlarını o belirler.

en.one: India's largest company in cleaning, personal care and food brands. The moat is wide; it waits at the gate because the price is very expensive.
en.business: Hindustan Unilever sells detergent, soap, shampoo, skin care, tea, coffee and packaged food. It delivers about 85 billion packs a year to about 9 million outlets. In the fiscal year that ended in March 2026 revenue was 637.6 billion rupees and the EBITDA margin 23.6%. It has 21 brands with annual sales above 10 billion rupees each.
en.moat_text: The moat is wide. The advantage comes from brands and distribution: 21 large brands and a network that reaches about 9 million outlets. Building the same network would take a competitor years and a large amount of capital. Pricing power shows in the margin: the EBITDA margin is in the 22-24% range. Real return on equity stayed between 12.0% and 19.6% in the last five fiscal years and was 15.2% in the last 12 months. The weak side: growth was feeble in the last two years; the company is looking for growth in the new brands it bought (Minimalist, OZiva). Real profitability is close to the thresholds of Wall 2.
en.mgmt: The parent, Unilever, holds 61.90% of the capital (September 2026). Most of the profit is paid out as dividends: 41 rupees per share for fiscal 2026, 96.3 billion rupees in total. The company has no net debt (net debt/EBITDA −0.54). The ice cream business was transferred to a separate company (Kwality Wall's) in the December 2025 quarter; Minimalist and OZiva were bought and Pureit was sold. Management plans to raise capital spending from 2% of revenue to 3%.
en.latest: 28 October 2026: In the July-September 2026 quarter revenue was 180.7 billion rupees. Underlying sales growth reported by the company was 15%, the highest in the last 14 quarters; sales volume rose 7%. EBITDA was 40.9 billion rupees (+8%) and the EBITDA margin 22.6% (1.4 points lower than a year earlier). Net profit was 28.0 billion rupees, the same as last year; excluding exceptional items it rose 9%. An interim dividend of 19 rupees per share was declared.
risks: Price: the P/E of 30.8 on the page is calculated with a profit that includes a one-off gain of about 46 billion rupees from the separation of the ice cream business. Without this gain the multiple is higher still (42.0 on Screener.in). There is no margin of safety.
Margin pressure: the EBITDA margin fell 1.4 points in the last quarter; input costs are high. Growth is coming from volume, and profit is not rising at the same pace.
The average real return on equity is at the threshold of Wall 2. If inflation rises or profit falls, the company can be eliminated at the quality wall.
New brands that sell online and quick-delivery apps can weaken the advantage that the distribution network provides.
The parent, Unilever, is the majority owner; it decides on dividends and acquisitions.

ORIANA.one: Güneş santrali ve batarya depolama müteahhidi. Kalite surlarını geçti; iş ihaleyle alınıyor, marj daralıyor. Hendek zayıf olduğu için 3. suru geçemedi.
ORIANA.business: Oriana Power (TrueRE markası) Hindistan'da güneş santralleri ve batarya depolama tesisleri kurar. Bir bölümünü müşteri için yapar; bir bölümünü kendi proje şirketlerinde kurup işletir, sonra yatırımcıya satar. Mart 2026'da biten mali yılda konsolide hasılat 18,1 milyar rupi (+%83,7), ana ortaklık net kârı 2,52 milyar rupi (+%59,1) oldu. Teslim edilen güneş gücü 835 MW'ın üzerinde; 700 MW'tan fazla güneş ve 1.000 MWh'ten fazla depolama yapım aşamasında. Yönetime göre bekleyen sipariş yaklaşık 70 milyar rupi.
ORIANA.moat_text: Hendek zayıf; şirket bu ölçütü geçemedi. İş ihale ve teklifle alınır. Yönetim Haziran 2026 toplantısında depolama ve müteahhitlik ihalelerinde saldırgan teklifler verildiğini, düşük fiyatlı ihalelerden çekildiğini söyledi. Üstünlük, proje geliştirme ile yapımı bir arada yürütmekten geliyor ve rakamda görünüyor: FAVÖK marjı yaklaşık %23, reel özsermaye kârlılığı son beş mali yılda %31,1 ile %58,0 arasında. Ama bu üstünlük kolay aşılır ve kısa bir geçmişe dayanıyor: hasılat Mart 2022'de biten yıldaki 1,2 milyar rupiden 18,1 milyar rupiye çıktı, net kâr marjı son yıl %16,06'dan %13,91'e indi, reel özsermaye kârlılığı %45,7'den %31,1'e geriledi. Fiyatı şirket değil ihale belirliyor.
ORIANA.mgmt: Kurucu ortakların payı %57,98 (Eylül 2026). Şirket NSE'nin KOBİ pazarında (Emerge) işlem görür; sonuçlarını yılda iki kez açıklar ve mali yılı mart sonunda biter. Temettü dağıtmıyor; kâr yeni projelere gidiyor. Borç büyüyor: toplam finansal borç 31 Mart 2026'da 5,09 milyar rupi (bir yıl önce 2,71 milyar), finansman gideri 629 milyon rupi (bir yıl önce 245 milyon). Faaliyet nakit akışı 3,37 milyar rupi, yatırım nakit çıkışı 5,06 milyar rupi. Yapı karmaşık: 74 bağlı ortaklık var; satılması planlanan 14'ü konsolide edilmiyor. Şirket ana işin yanında yeşil amonyak ve hidrojen yatırımlarına giriyor. Eylül 2026'da her pay beşe bölündü (nominal değer 10 rupiden 2 rupiye). Denetçi görüşü olumlu.
ORIANA.latest: 28 Mayıs 2026: Mart 2026'da biten mali yılda konsolide hasılat 18,1 milyar rupi (+%83,7), FAVÖK 4,25 milyar rupi (+%73,4), ana ortaklık net kârı 2,52 milyar rupi (+%59,1). İkinci yarıda (Ekim 2025-Mart 2026) net kâr 1,31 milyar rupi; artış %19,0'a yavaşladı. Tek seferlik kalem yok. Yönetim, yaklaşık 238 MW'lık işler durumdaki güneş santrallerinin Actis'e satışının bu yıla yetişmediğini ve kârın beklentinin altında kaldığını söyledi. Haberlere göre satışın ilk bölümleri Eylül 2026 sonunda tamamlandı: 110 MWp için işletme değeri 5,01 milyar rupi. Nisan-Eylül 2026 sonuçları 13 Kasım 2026 itibarıyla açıklanmamıştı.
risks: Kâr büyümesi yavaşlıyor ve marj daralıyor: son yarı yılda net kâr %19,0 arttı (yılın tamamında %59,1), net kâr marjı %16,06'dan %13,91'e indi. Yönetim ihalelerde saldırgan fiyatlama olduğunu söylüyor.
Kârın bir bölümü kendi kurduğu santrallerin satışına bağlı. Satış gecikince kâr o dönem gelmiyor; gelince de o dönemin kârını yükseltiyor. Actis satışı Nisan-Eylül 2026 dönemine düşecek.
Borç ve işletme sermayesi hızla büyüyor: finansal borç bir yılda 2,71 milyar rupiden 5,09 milyar rupiye, ticari alacak 3,94 milyar rupiden 6,71 milyar rupiye çıktı.
İş kamu ihalelerine, şebeke bağlantısına ve teşvik kurallarına bağlı. Yönetim arazi, bağlantı ve onay gecikmelerini, kur ve hammadde maliyetini risk olarak sayıyor.
KOBİ pazarında işlem görüyor: sonuçlar yılda iki kez açıklanır, tablolar eski Hint muhasebe standartlarıyla (AS) hazırlanır ve 14 bağlı ortaklık konsolide edilmez.

en.one: Solar and battery storage contractor. Passed the quality walls; work is won by tender, margins are narrowing. Weak moat, so it failed Wall 3.
en.business: Oriana Power (TrueRE brand) builds solar plants and battery storage facilities in India. It builds part of them for customers; part it builds and runs in its own project companies and later sells to investors. In the fiscal year that ended in March 2026, consolidated revenue was 18.1 billion rupees (+83.7%) and net profit attributable to owners was 2.52 billion rupees (+59.1%). Solar capacity delivered is above 835 MW; more than 700 MW of solar and more than 1,000 MWh of storage are under construction. Management puts the unexecuted order book at about 70 billion rupees.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; the company did not pass this criterion. Work is won by tender and by bid. At the June 2026 meeting management said that bidding in storage and contracting tenders was aggressive and that it had stepped back from low-priced tenders. The advantage comes from doing project development and construction together, and it shows in the numbers: the EBITDA margin is about 23% and real return on equity was between 31.1% and 58.0% in the last five fiscal years. But this advantage is easy to overcome and rests on a short record: revenue went from 1.2 billion rupees in the year that ended in March 2022 to 18.1 billion rupees, the net profit margin fell from 16.06% to 13.91% last year, and real return on equity fell from 45.7% to 31.1%. The price is set by the tender, not by the company.
en.mgmt: The founders hold 57.98% (September 2026). The company trades on the NSE's SME platform (Emerge); it reports results twice a year and its fiscal year ends in March. It pays no dividend; profit goes into new projects. Debt is growing: total borrowings were 5.09 billion rupees on 31 March 2026 (2.71 billion a year earlier) and finance costs were 629 million rupees (245 million a year earlier). Operating cash flow was 3.37 billion rupees and investing cash outflow 5.06 billion rupees. The structure is complex: there are 74 subsidiaries, and 14 that are planned for sale are not consolidated. Alongside its main business the company is entering green ammonia and hydrogen investments. In September 2026 each share was split into five (face value from 10 rupees to 2 rupees). The auditor's opinion is unmodified.
en.latest: 28 May 2026: In the fiscal year that ended in March 2026, consolidated revenue was 18.1 billion rupees (+83.7%), EBITDA 4.25 billion rupees (+73.4%) and net profit attributable to owners 2.52 billion rupees (+59.1%). In the second half (October 2025-March 2026) net profit was 1.31 billion rupees; growth slowed to 19.0%. There were no one-off items. Management said the sale of about 238 MW of operating solar plants to Actis did not close within the year and that profit fell short of its expectation. According to news reports the first parts of the sale closed at the end of September 2026: an enterprise value of 5.01 billion rupees for 110 MWp. Results for April-September 2026 had not been published as of 13 November 2026.
risks: Profit growth is slowing and the margin is narrowing: net profit rose 19.0% in the latest half-year (59.1% for the full year) and the net profit margin fell from 16.06% to 13.91%. Management says pricing in tenders is aggressive.

Part of the profit depends on selling plants the company built itself. When a sale is delayed the profit does not arrive in that period; when it closes it lifts that period's profit. The Actis sale will fall in the April-September 2026 period.
Debt and working capital are growing fast: in one year borrowings went from 2.71 billion rupees to 5.09 billion rupees and trade receivables from 3.94 billion rupees to 6.71 billion rupees.
The business depends on public tenders, grid connection and incentive rules. Management lists delays in land, connectivity and approvals, the exchange rate and input costs as risks.
It trades on the SME platform: results come twice a year, the statements are prepared under the older Indian accounting standards (AS), and 14 subsidiaries are not consolidated.
